title: UK 6 GHz standard-power Wi-Fi under AFC
research_origin: US FCC 6 GHz rules (2020) introducing AFC-controlled standard-power Wi-Fi, building on earlier geolocation-database spectrum sharing
research_what: Automated frequency coordination, a database-driven control that lets higher-power Wi-Fi share 6 GHz with incumbent users, was first enabled by US regulators and then adopted in Canada.
change_what: UK regulations (SI 2026/1132) licence-exempt standard-power Wi-Fi across 5925–7125 MHz for AFC-controlled devices, coming into force on 10 November 2026; Ofcom AFC provider registration opened from 1 September 2026.

title: Otarmeni: first dual-AAV gene therapy for deafness
research_origin: Dual-AAV OTOF gene therapy in Otof-knockout mice (Akil et al., PNAS 2019; Al-Moyed et al., EMBO Mol Med 2019), later developed as DB-OTO by Akouos and Regeneron
research_what: Mouse studies showed that splitting the large OTOF gene across two AAV vectors could restore hearing in a model of OTOF deafness.
change_what: The FDA granted accelerated approval to Regeneron's Otarmeni on 23 April 2026, the first gene therapy for genetic hearing loss, given as a one-time dose into the cochlea.

title: ER-100: first human trial of partial cell reprogramming
research_origin: Partial reprogramming work derived from Yamanaka factors (2006), with Ocampo et al., Cell 2016, and Lu et al., Nature 2020 on optic nerve regeneration; developed as ER-100 by Life Biosciences
research_what: Partial, cyclic expression of Yamanaka reprogramming factors was shown to reverse ageing features in mice, and later to restore vision in mouse optic nerve injury and glaucoma models.
change_what: Life Biosciences announced on 9 June 2026 that it had dosed the first participant in its phase 1 trial of ER-100 for optic neuropathies such as glaucoma, the first human use of a partial-reprogramming therapy.

title: Sodium-ion batteries in mass-produced vehicles
research_origin: CATL sodium-ion R&D programme from 2016; first-generation sodium-ion cell introduced July 2021 (160 Wh/kg)
research_what: CATL began research and development of sodium-ion cells as a lithium-free alternative chemistry, and introduced a first-generation cell in 2021.
change_what: In February 2026 CATL and Changan unveiled what CATL called the first mass-production passenger car with sodium-ion batteries. CATL also launched a mass-produced sodium battery for light commercial vehicles in early 2026.

title: Sulfonamide drugs (Prontosil)
research_origin: IG Farben/Bayer dye-based antibacterial programme: Klarer and Mietzsch synthesis (1932) and Domagk's 1935 paper on bacterial chemotherapy
research_what: IG Farben/Bayer chemists made the azo dye Prontosil in 1932, and Gerhard Domagk found it protected mice against streptococcal infection.
change_what: Prontosil was patented and went on sale in 1935 as the first drug to cure systemic bacterial infections, with clinical use in Germany, France, Britain and the US from 1935 to 1936.

title: Yellow fever 17D vaccine
research_origin: Rockefeller Foundation International Health Division programme led by Max Theiler and Hugh Smith; three J. Exp. Med. papers in 1937
research_what: Max Theiler at the Rockefeller Foundation worked from 1930 to weaken yellow fever virus by repeated passage in tissue culture so it could immunise without causing disease.
change_what: The attenuated 17D strain was first produced in 1937, field-tested in Brazil with Rockefeller Foundation funding, then licensed and manufactured at scale.

title: Computer passwords (CTSS)
research_origin: MIT Compatible Time-Sharing System (CTSS), led by Fernando Corbató, first demonstrated in November 1961
research_what: MIT researchers building a time-sharing system needed a way to give each user private files, so they added a per-user password check.
change_what: CTSS put per-user password login into live use on a shared MIT computer, the first widely credited password system on a computer and the model for later multi-user logins.

title: Protection rings (Multics)
research_origin: R. M. Graham's 1967 protection-ring proposal within the MIT/Bell Labs/GE Multics project, whose design was laid out in 1964-1967
research_what: Graham proposed concentric rings of decreasing privilege to isolate programs and data inside a shared computer utility, within the Multics design.
change_what: Multics, which used protection rings first in software and later in hardware, was in operation by 1969. Hitachi built a hardware ring system in 1968, and rings later appeared in mainstream processors.

title: Coal-to-liquid fuel: Bergius hydrogenation at Leuna
research_origin: Friedrich Bergius's 1913 German patent on high-pressure coal hydrogenation; BASF's Matthias Pier later adapted it to industrial scale.
research_what: Friedrich Bergius patented a way to turn coal into liquid fuel by hydrogenating it at high temperature and pressure.
change_what: IG Farben's Leuna works began commercial hydrogenation of lignite on 1 April 1927, giving the first industrial-scale synthetic petrol.

title: Reflection seismograph for oil exploration
research_origin: J. Clarence Karcher's June 1921 reflection field test at Belle Isle, Oklahoma City, building on Reginald Fessenden's 1917 patent.
research_what: Karcher's team recorded the first reflection seismograph field test near Oklahoma City in June 1921, building on Fessenden's 1917 patent work.
change_what: Amerada's drilling in the Seminole area of Oklahoma in 1928 produced the first oil well located using a reflection seismograph, after seismic refraction had found Texas salt-dome oil in 1924.

title: Project Diana: first radar echo from the Moon
research_origin: US Army Signal Corps Evans Signal Laboratory, wartime radar development (SCR-271), Project Diana planning 1945
research_what: US Army Signal Corps radar engineers at Evans Signal Laboratory adapted wartime long-range radar (the modified SCR-271 set) to try to reach the Moon.
change_what: On 10 January 1946 the Project Diana team detected radar echoes returning from the Moon after about 2.5 seconds, the first experiment in radar astronomy and the first active probe of another celestial body.

title: Electron microscope (matter-wave imaging)
research_origin: Louis de Broglie's 1924 doctoral thesis on matter waves, followed by Ruska and Knoll's 1931 electron lens and microscope prototype at TU Berlin
research_what: Louis de Broglie proposed that electrons behave as waves with very short wavelengths, which implied that electron imaging could resolve far finer detail than light.
change_what: Siemens delivered its first serially produced commercial electron microscope, the Siemens Super Microscope, to I.G. Farben in Frankfurt-Höchst in late 1939.
